summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia, chronic obstructive lung disease, and a history of recurrent pneumonia and UTIs, was admitted with shortness of breath, fever, and hypoxia. She was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, sensitive only to meropenem, and aspiration pneumonia with MRSA involvement. She was initially managed in the MICU with vancomycin and meropenem, along with supportive care for respiratory failure. Due to difficult IV access, a tunneled central line was placed after failed PICC attempts. A video swallow study confirmed aspiration with thin and nectar-thick liquids, leading to dietary modifications. Her condition improved with treatment, oxygen requirements returned to baseline, and she was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of IV antibiotics via home health. Follow-up was arranged with pulmonology and gastroenterology.
